title: Double indentation for script tag in html

labels.name: syntax
labels.description: regex syntax or non-regex parsing, lpeg, grammars

labels.name: needs:vim-patch
labels.description: upstream issue that must be fixed in Vim first

body:
### Neovim Version

v0.5.0

### Operating system/version:

Ubuntu 20.04

### Terminal name/version:

xfce4-terminal

### TERM environment variable

xterm-256color

### Installation

appimage

### Steps to reproduce

I am starting from a simple HTML `index.html` file containing only a pair of `<html>` tags.

```html
<html>
</html>
```

I am using neovim v0.5.0, downloaded from the appimage, and I am opening the above HTML file with:

```
nvim.appimage -u NORC index.html
```

Then, I put my cursor on the opening tag `<html>` and go to insert mode at the next line using `o`. Then I start to type `<script`. But when I add the closing character `>`, the tag gets pushed one level of indentation to the right.

To me, this is not supposed to happen. And if I repeat the exact same steps with neovim v0.4.4, I don’t have the problem. The `<script>` stays where it is.

See the problem in action.

![nvim_script_indent](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3764103/129983265-924b1a27-1309-41fa-9f2e-87b290f2409b.gif)

I don’t know if it can help, but there were 4 commits altering `runtime/indent/html.vim` between v0.4.4 and v0.5.0.

```
$ git log --oneline v0.4.4..v0.5.0 -- runtime/indent/html.vim
2081504a3 vim-patch:942db23c9cb7
b1cd67b62 vim-patch:4072ba571bab
27fb03f5a vim-patch:7ff78465f705
7c6ca6fed vim-patch:73fef33014db
```

### Vim

Bug happens with vim -u DEFAULTS

### Expected behavior

When closing the tag with `>`, I am expecting to have this output (`<script>` does not move, and stay at its level of indentation).

```html
<html>
        <script>
</html>
```

### Actual behavior

Instead, I have this output (with 2 indentation levels).

```html
<html>
                <script>
</html>
```
